realizations.description: A live window opens immediately after possession is lost; the pressing team attempts to regain inside that window; if the team escapes the counter-press, they earn a restart or continuation bonus.
realizations.design_intent: Live counter-press window creates a contested advantage on every possession change; the team losing the ball decides whether to commit to the press or recover shape; the team gaining the ball decides whether to exploit the disorganized pressure or recirculate safely.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use the counter-press window as a scoring incentive; escaping the press earns a bonus; failing to regain inside the window means the opponent gets a live advantage and the defending team must recover shape.
realizations.setup_guidance: Coach calls out 'press' (or starts a timer) the moment possession changes.; Typical counter-press window: 5 seconds. Pressing team must regain within that window for the press to count as successful.; If the window expires without regain, the team in possession earns a restart bonus or free continuation.
realizations.contraindications: The window invites counter-pressing as a live choice — not a requirement. Teams adapt based on opponent readiness, pressure cover, and their own recovery shape.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Counter-press window creates a contested advantage moment; the team that loses possession decides whether to commit to the press immediately or protect the deeper zone; the team with the ball chooses whether to exploit the disorganized pressure or secure possession.

realizations.description: A goal or score attempt counts only when the team completes a connected combination of passes first; defending team can reset the count by winning possession or forcing a turnover under pressure.
realizations.design_intent: Combination gate creates a live possession problem under opponent pressure; defending teams read the passing rhythm and choose whether to press early or delay and force the ball wide; attacking teams adapt support structure and spacing to complete combinations and unlock the score attempt.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use the combination gate as a scoring incentive; teams choose when the picture is open to attempt goal versus when recirculation opens more space and a better option.
realizations.setup_guidance: Goal/score attempts only count when the attacking team has completed a minimum of 4-6 connected passes in their half (adjust by age/ability).; Pass count resets when possession is lost or the ball leaves play.; Coach tracks the count visibly (count out loud or use a counter).
realizations.contraindications: The combination is an ecological scoring gate — not a technique exercise. Teams adapt their support angles and spacing to complete combinations under live opposition.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Combination gate creates a visible build-up problem; teams decide when the picture is ready to commit to goal versus when recirculating and finding a better lane is the right choice; defenders choose whether to press the combination early or delay and protect space.

realizations.description: A penetrating pass or forward run into a scoring area counts only when a supporting player has occupied the required lane or channel; defending team reads support lane occupation and decides whether to press the ball or track the run.
realizations.design_intent: Support lane requirement creates a visible spatial game problem; the free player decides when to enter the lane based on defensive coverage; the ball carrier adapts timing of the forward pass based on lane occupation and pressure; defending team reacts to both the ball and the lane to deny the penetrating option.

realizations.setup_guidance: Mark a support lane (typically a half-space corridor between center and wide channels) with cones.; Forward passes or penetrating runs into the scoring area only count when a supporting player has entered the marked lane before the pass.; The lane is a reference area — players choose when to enter and when not to, based on the live picture.
realizations.contraindications: The lane is an ecological condition — players read lane occupation and decide when to play forward based on the live picture, not on instruction.

realizations.setup_guidance: Divide the field into 3-4 defined zones (e.g., build-up / mid / attacking; or left / center / right channels).; Mark zone boundaries clearly with cones or discs.; Players move freely between zones; the structure exists to make zone transitions visible, not to limit movement.
realizations.contraindications: Zones shape the environment — they do not restrict how players choose to act within or between zones.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Zone boundaries create visible reference points for pressure reads; players decide when the picture is open to progress into the next zone, support from depth, or switch the attack across zones.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: neutral player; joker; overload player; extra player; support player; floating player; always with possession; attacking neutral; free player; play through the neutral; use the joker; numbers up; find the free player; use the extra player
realizations.description: One or more neutral players join the team in possession creating a live numerical overload; defending team reads the support angles and decides whether to press the free player or protect the deeper zone.
realizations.design_intent: Numerical advantage from the neutral player creates visible pressure differences and support options; teams read the picture to decide when the free option opens space or invites the penetrating pass.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use neutral player structure to invite overload exploitation; defenders decide how to cover the extra option while attackers choose the best moment to use the numerical advantage.
realizations.setup_guidance: Designate one or two neutral players (wear contrasting bibs).; Neutrals always play with the team in possession, creating a permanent numerical advantage for whichever side has the ball.; Adjust team numbers accordingly (e.g., for 15 players: 6v6 + 3 neutrals, or 7v7 + 1 neutral).
realizations.contraindications: Neutral player creates structural overload — not a coaching script. Players choose when and how to use the numerical advantage based on the live pressure picture.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Neutral player changes the space, support angles, and passing options for both sides; attackers decide whether to use the overload immediately or recirculate to find a better lane.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: include the goalkeeper; build through the goalkeeper; goalkeeper in possession; play back to the keeper; goalkeeper involved; use the keeper; play out from the back; goalkeeper support; build from the back; live goalkeeper; goalkeeper as an option; involve the keeper; reset through the keeper; use the goalkeeper as support
realizations.description: Goalkeeper is active in all phases as a live option for distribution, support, and recovery; attacking team reads the space behind defensive lines and decides when to pressure the target area under live goal threat.
realizations.design_intent: Live goalkeeper creates a real target and real pressure on attacking and defending decisions; space behind the defensive line, support angles, and finishing windows are all live based on GK position and defensive recovery.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use goalkeeper inclusion to invite realistic build-up and finishing pressure; teams read GK positioning and space behind the last line before deciding to attack or recirculate.
realizations.setup_guidance: Goalkeepers in their normal goal positions at each end of the field.; GKs are live during all phases — they distribute, save, and count as outfield support when team is building from the back.; Use full-size or scaled goals depending on field dimensions.
realizations.contraindications: GK participation is structural — players choose when and how to involve the GK as they would in a real match, not on instruction.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: GK inclusion adds a live pressure reference on both sides; attackers read the goalkeeper position and support angles to choose finishing windows; defenders use GK as a support option to escape pressure.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: small-sided area; tight space; compact area; reduce the space; smaller field; play in a tight area; compress the space; limited space; close quarters; confined area; make the field smaller; play under pressure; play in traffic; solve the pressure; deal with tight spaces
realizations.description: Compact pitch proportions place teams in tight space with reduced time; all attacking and defending actions occur under live pressure within a smaller area; spatial awareness and timing shape every decision.
realizations.design_intent: Compact area forces faster reads and tighter support decisions; space is at a premium and teams adapt their timing, passing angles, and movement based on the live pressure picture.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use small area structure to sharpen decision-making under pressure; players read pressure and support in tight zones before choosing the next action.
realizations.setup_guidance: Reduce the field to a compact area (typical: 30-40m x 25-35m for 8-12 players).; Tight boundaries increase pressure cycles without changing the basic game form.; Adjust dimensions based on player age and ability — smaller for tighter pressure, larger to ease cognitive load.
realizations.contraindications: Space reduction is structural — it creates representative pressure through environment, not scripted actions.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Reduced space intensifies pressure cycles; teams read opponent pressure and support angles in a tighter window before choosing to secure possession, switch play, or escape into space.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: read the picture; what's on?; which option is on; keep your options open; don't decide early; play what you see; late target; changing target; variable target; attack the open target; choose the best option; adapt to the picture; scan before you play; recognize the live target; don't pre-plan; don't lock in; read before committing; keep options open
realizations.description: Which target or scoring option is live is revealed late or changes during play, so teams must read the current picture rather than commit to a pre-planned route.
realizations.design_intent: Delaying or varying which target is live forces perception of the live picture over pre-planned routes; teams adapt the direction of their progression to the target that becomes available.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use a late or changing live-target rule so teams read the current picture before committing to a route.
realizations.setup_guidance: Mark 2-3 possible targets/gates (e.g. across the far line or at multiple edges).; Which target is live is revealed only after play crosses a trigger line, or switches on a coach cue during play.; All targets stay physically available so the choice remains open; only the LIVE one scores.
realizations.contraindications: The variability shapes information availability, not behavior — players choose how to exploit whichever target is live.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Players cannot lock onto a pre-chosen target; they keep options open and perceive which target has become live under pressure. Scanning emerges as one adaptation, it is not required.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: multiple goals; two goals; three goals; attack the open goal; which goal is open; find the free target; choose the best goal; scan the goals; switch goals; attack what's available; recognize the open option; don't force one goal; read which is open; scan the targets; where's the space?
realizations.description: Two or more goals/targets are live at once and defended differently; the attack must perceive which is least protected at this moment rather than attack a single known target.
realizations.design_intent: Several live targets create a perception problem: the attack reads which target is least protected now and the defense reorganizes to cover, so advantage comes from recognizing the open option, not from a rehearsed route.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Use multiple simultaneously-live goals so the attack perceives which is open rather than attacking one fixed target.
realizations.setup_guidance: Set 2-3 small goals/targets spread across the end line (or at multiple edges of the field).; All targets are live to score at the same time; defenders cannot cover all equally.; Field width keeps the targets far enough apart that the attack must perceive and exploit which is open.
realizations.contraindications: The multiple targets shape what must be perceived — players choose which to attack; no specific target or movement is prescribed.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Multiple simultaneous targets distribute the information across the field; players read which target the defense has left open and the defense shifts to cover, so the open option keeps moving.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: blind side; attack the blind side; arrive unseen; back shoulder; behind the defender; exploit the blind side; defender can't see you; arrive out of sight; unseen run; attack from behind; back-post run; lose your defender; lose your marker; disappear from view; arrive late; blind-side run
realizations.description: Advantage created from outside a defender's field of view (a run or pass arriving from the blind side) is worth more, rewarding the relationship rather than any specific movement.
realizations.design_intent: Information out of a defender's view is the resource: advantage created from the blind side counts more, so players perceive defender orientation and exploit unseen space — many movements satisfy it.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Reward advantage gained from a defender's blind side so players read body orientation and exploit where defenders cannot see.
realizations.setup_guidance: Play toward a real goal/target with active defenders and (ideally) a goalkeeper.; Advantage or a goal created from a blind-side relationship (a run or pass arriving from outside the defender's view) is worth more (e.g. counts double).; Do not specify the run — any action that exploits a defender's blind side qualifies.
realizations.contraindications: Rewards the OUTCOME of using a blind-side relationship — there are many ways to create one — never a specific movement pattern.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: Players read where defenders are not looking and exploit the blind side; defenders adapt their body orientation and scanning. The reward is for the perceptual relationship, not a prescribed run.

realizations.coach_vocabulary: different restart; variable restart; unpredictable restart; new picture every time; don't rehearse; organize live; fresh picture; read the restart; different starting point; varied entry; restart from anywhere; adapt to the picture; expect the unexpected; organize on the move; read the new picture; different starting picture; can't rehearse
realizations.description: Each repetition restarts from a variable, not-pre-known entry, so neither team can rehearse a picture; both must read and organize live. Scoped to variable-entry pictures, not reaction or signal-guessing tasks.
realizations.design_intent: A variable entry removes the pre-set picture each repetition; teams cannot rehearse, so they perceive and organize to whatever situation the restart presents — mirroring how real restarts and transitions arrive unpredictably.
realizations.suggested_constraint_prompt: Restart from a variable, last-moment entry so neither team can pre-arrange a picture and both must read the live situation.
realizations.setup_guidance: Prepare several possible entry points/gates around the field (e.g. 3-4 served-in locations).; Which entry is used is chosen at the last moment, so neither team knows the starting picture in advance.; Keep play continuous once the ball enters; the variability is only in WHERE/HOW it starts, never a behavior the coach calls.
realizations.contraindications: Shapes information by removing a pre-set picture — it must NOT become a coach-signal-guessing or reaction-time task. The variability is in the entry, not a behavior cue.
realizations.provenance: Extracted from TEST_LIBRARY_V0_CONSTRAINTS and TEST_LIBRARY_V0_ENVIRONMENTAL_MANIPULATIONS via extract-soccer-realizations.ts
realizations.notes: The entry point/side is chosen at the last moment, so the starting picture differs each rep; teams perceive and organize to the live situation instead of running a rehearsed pattern.
